svg.style: background: transparent; background-color: transparent; color-scheme: light;

g.text: anything else becomes an empty href
Everything the backend can emit, the complete tag vocabulary:
p · h1..h6 id="" · pre · code class="language-" · blockquote · ul · ol · li · table · thead · tbody · tr · th · td
hr · em · strong · a href="" · img src="" alt="" · br · span class="math | tok-kw | tok-str | tok-com | tok-num | tok-var"
Every byte that came from the document reaches the output through escape_byte, never verbatim.
The classic verified-compiler split: the messy frontend is off the shelf and
unverified, only the backend is proved. That is not a compromise, because the
safety theorem quantifies over every Ast: whatever the parser produces, the
renderer cannot emit input-derived markup. The parser can be buggy, hostile,
or replaced, and the property survives, since it was never about the parser.
raw HTML events, dropped by adapt.rs: no Ast node exists for them
The middle column is what the theorems quantify over: whatever lands there, the right column can carry markup only from the fixed vocabulary.
